events.title: A CARD UNDER THE DOOR
events.text: A woman with magenta hair and a too-wide smile leans on your doorframe. 'Wire. I move things that aren't supposed to move. You'll want what I sell.'

outcomes.text: Wire taps the card twice. 'Ask for the den behind the noodle stall. Bring cash.'
'They all say that once.' She leaves the card anyway.

events.title: WIRE AGAIN
events.text: 'Still cutting with scrap? Last offer, ripper.'

outcomes.text: 'Smart.'
She shrugs and melts into the rain.

events.title: INSPECTION
events.text: Inspector Moor of the Civic Medical Board steps in, scanner already humming. 'Routine check. Unless you'd rather it wasn't routine.'

outcomes.text: The scanner goes quiet. 'Clean as a whistle. See you next quarter.'

success.text: She squints at the forgery... and nods.

outcomes.text: She confiscates one item of contraband and leaves satisfied.

events.title: SUSPICIOUS CUSTOMER
events.text: A hooded man won't give a name. He wants a corporate tracking chip cut out of his shoulder. Tonight.

outcomes.text: The chip pings once in your tray, then dies. He's gone before it stops.
He leaves without a word. A drone hovers outside a minute later.

events.title: HOT CHROME
events.text: A jittery runner opens a duffel bag: still-warm implants with corporate serials. 'Three hundred for the lot, no questions.'

outcomes.text: You stash an implant. The rest are scrap.
Corporate security thanks you. The Rustline crews won't.
He swears at you and runs.

events.title: EMERGENCY
events.text: Someone hammers the door: a Rustline kid with a knife wound and failing chrome, dumped by friends who already ran.

outcomes.text: You drag him onto the table. Fast pay if he lives.
Word travels fast in the lower levels.

events.title: SEALED CASE
events.text: Wire slides a sealed case across your table. 'One token. Could be junk. Could be military. I genuinely don't know.'

outcomes.text: Inside, something hums.
'Your loss.'

events.title: A FAVOUR FOR ROOK
events.text: Rook wants a kill-switch slipped into a rival lieutenant's arm during his next checkup. 'Four hundred. And my gratitude.'

outcomes.text: It's a small chip. It weighs a lot.
'Shame. I liked you.'

events.title: PROTECTION
events.text: A big man with a chrome jaw blocks your doorway. 'Rook. This block is Rustline. We keep it quiet for people we like.'

outcomes.text: 'Good. Nobody bothers you now. Mostly.'
'Your call. The streets are dangerous.'

events.title: RECALL NOTICE
events.text: A recall bulletin scrolls across your terminal: one of your stocked implants is from a defective batch.

outcomes.text: You strip it for parts.
Next operation will be riskier.

events.title: POWER OUTAGE
events.text: The block grid dies. Your lamp flickers on the emergency battery.

outcomes.text: The generator coughs to life.
Next operation: complications more likely.

events.title: EQUIPMENT FAILURE
events.text: Your instrument tray's sterilizer shorts out with a smell of burnt plastic.

outcomes.text: Fixed. Mostly.
You patch it with salvaged parts.
Your next two operations will be less precise.

events.title: DRONE OUTSIDE
events.text: A matte-black Aegis drone has been hovering at the end of your alley for an hour.

outcomes.text: It drifts away, confused.
A clerical error loses your file.
It takes pictures. Lots of pictures.

events.title: NO PAY
events.text: Your last customer's 'friend' comes back: they won't pay the second half. 'What are you gonna do about it?'

fail.text: He laughs and walks out. People heard.

outcomes.text: Word gets around that you're fair. Or soft.
Rook's crew collects. They keep a cut of your goodwill.

events.title: SURPLUS SUPPLIES
events.text: A hospital orderly sells 'expired' surgical supplies out of a van.

outcomes.text: Expired yesterday. Fine.
The van drives off.

events.title: THE OLD SURGEON
events.text: A gray-haired woman watches you clean up. 'I was a corporate surgeon for twenty years. For 400 I'll show you what they never put in manuals.'

outcomes.text: You learn more in one night than in a year. (+1 skill point)
'Suit yourself. I'll be around.'

events.title: AN ANGRY VISIT
events.text: Family of a patient you failed is at your door. They want answers, or money.

outcomes.text: They leave, still angry, but quiet.
They promise to tell everyone.

events.title: BACK ON YOUR TABLE
events.text: A recent patient staggers in, sweating, the fresh incision red and hot. Your work is failing. Everyone on the block is watching how you handle it.

outcomes.text: You reopen, clean it out and send them home grateful.
They pay. They also tell everyone they had to.
They collapse two doors down. The street remembers.

events.title: STATIC FEVER
events.text: News feed: a patient with too much chrome had a neural break on the transit line. Your name is being whispered.

outcomes.text: Overloading people has consequences.

events.title: THE FILAMENT
events.text: Bram is still under. You lift one of the silver filaments out of the wound with the fine tweezers. It moves. Slowly, like it's feeling for the nerve it lost.

wall.title: Vial, cold box
wall.text: A silver filament from Bram Okoye. Label: ?

outcomes.text: It goes in a vial at the back of the cold box. You write a question mark on the label and nothing else.
He laughs it off. 'Free medicine, doc. When does that ever happen down here?' Then he stops laughing.
Not your business. You close him up and wash your hands twice.

events.title: THE MOTHER'S QUESTION
events.text: Wren sits on the edge of the table, perfectly still, waiting to be told she can stand. Her mother holds your sleeve. 'Is it the tonic? Did they do something to her?'

outcomes.text: You tell her what you saw: silver, growing, and nobody's name on it. She doesn't cry. She asks where the van parks.
'I don't know.' It's even true, mostly. She thanks you anyway, which is worse.
Saline and a vitamin patch, a hundred and twenty credits. She pays in coins. Wren says 'thank you, doctor' exactly the way she was told to.

events.title: THE HANDSHAKE LOG
events.text: Pike's old port kept a log nobody was meant to read. Three thousand requests from LYR-THREAD v0.9, all granted, none by Pike. It's on your screen now. It could be on anybody's.

outcomes.text: You print it, fold it twice and pin it behind the wall where the damp can't reach.
Gone. Pike's port is clean, your hands are clean, and somewhere a server notices nothing.
Wire pays before you finish the sentence. That should worry you more than it does.

events.title: WHAT DO YOU TELL THE CREWS?
events.text: Spit pulls his jacket back on over the new plating. 'Mother thinks the van's a gift. Quiet boys don't get shot. You gonna tell her what it really is?'

outcomes.text: You give Spit a message for Rook, not Mother. Rook will know what to do with it. Or he won't.
'Not my crew, not my business.' Spit nods like he expected it, and goes.

events.title: THE CLOSED FILES
events.text: Hester blinks at the new focus, reads the far wall, then reads you. 'Forty files, doctor. All closed by the same code. If someone asked me for copies, I'd have to say no.' She doesn't say no.

wall.title: Laundry bag
wall.text: Forty closed seizure files, Civic Medical Board.

outcomes.text: They arrive two nights later in a laundry bag, under the towels.
'People who read those files get transferred, Hester. Then they get forgotten.' She nods. She'll keep looking.

events.title: BED 14
events.text: The job you were paid for is done. The lattice is still in her, woven into the nerve that carries her voice. Getting it out is hours of work nobody pays for, and Lyra will know whose hands did it. On her wrist, a number with no name.

wall.title: Bed 14
wall.text: Sable Ndiaye walked out singing. Lattice in a jar.

outcomes.text: Four hours. Two supplies. At the end there's a grey knot of wire in the tray, and Sable is saying her own name like she's tasting it.

choices.label: LET HER GO AS SHE IS

outcomes.text: You give her a coat and the back door. She doesn't look back. You're not sure she can.
A polite voice thanks you for your cooperation. The car is outside before you've hung up.

events.title: STEADY
events.text: Bram's hands lie on the sheet exactly where you put them. The lattice has your servo's wiring wrapped in it like ivy on a fence. Pulling it could give him back. It could also take the rest.

wall.title: Bram Okoye
wall.text: Crane. Got up on his own.

success.text: It comes out in one long, horrible piece. An hour later Bram swears at you, unprompted. You've never been happier to be sworn at.

wall.title: Bram Okoye
wall.text: Crane. The thread took him with it.

fail.text: It doesn't let go. Neither does he, not for a long minute. Then he does.

outcomes.text: You turn the light down and sit with him a while. He thanks you for the chair. He'd thank you for anything now.
